column3: automations.revision floors at the wall clock: it starts at Date.now() on boot and each change sets max(revision + 1, Date.now()). Nothing is stored and no migration is added
column4: Deviation from 'persist it in the same row write': automation.delete writes no row a counter could ride on, so a stored counter costs one extra row write per change, a delete included. Clients compare the revision only for change, and a value floored at the wall clock never repeats across an eviction. The only exception would be more than one change per millisecond sustained up to the eviction. Bosun accepted this in place of a stored counter: the revision still rises across a reboot, with no migration and no extra row write. Caveat: it depends on the wall clock never moving backwards across a restart
